title: The 'My Brain Doesn't Write' Reframe Script Bank
howToUse: This is your ready-to-reach-for script bank for the specific moment writing stops — not a lesson on mindset, but pre-written sentences you read, say out loud, and get back to the page with. Keep it open in a second tab whenever you're working on copy. Each tool maps to a different stuck moment: the blank page, the rewrite spiral, and the post-publish regret. Use whichever section matches where you're stuck right now.
promise: These seventeen scripts hand you the exact words to redirect the "my brain doesn't write" conviction the moment it surfaces, so you stay in the session and finish the copy.

Find the section that names your current stuck moment. Read the script. Say it out loud if you can. Then return to the document without opening a new tab, googling anything, or asking anyone.

tools.name: The Stuck-Moment Triage Worksheet
tools.instructions: Fill in the four fields the next time you hit resistance in a writing session — it tells you exactly which script from the bank to reach for.
tools.content:
## The Stuck-Moment Triage Worksheet

A four-question worksheet that names your exact stuck moment and points you to the right script. Fill it in as you are, in the session, before you close the tab.

---

**Step 1 — Name the moment (circle one)**

- Blank page — nothing written yet
- Rewrite spiral — I've rewritten the same sentence or section more than three times
- Post-publish regret — it's live and I wish it weren't
- Mid-session shutdown — I was writing and suddenly stopped

---

**Step 2 — Name what the voice in your head just said**

*(Write it word for word. Don't clean it up.)*

[WRITE THE EXACT THOUGHT HERE]

---

**Step 3 — Match it to a script category**

| What the voice said | Script section to reach for |
|---|---|
| "I don't know where to start" | Section 1 — Blank Page (Scripts 1–6) |
| "This sounds nothing like me" | Section 1 — Blank Page (Script 4 or 5) |
| "I've already rewritten this four times" | Section 2 — Rewrite Spiral (Scripts 7–12) |
| "Other coaches write so naturally" | Section 2 — Rewrite Spiral (Script 10) |
| "I shouldn't have published that" | Section 3 — Post-Publish (Scripts 13–17) |
| "My audience is going to think I'm a fraud" | Section 3 — Post-Publish (Script 15 or 16) |

---

**Step 4 — Record what happened after you used the script**

*(One sentence. Did you get back to the document? Did the freeze lift? What did you write next?)*

[WRITE WHAT HAPPENED NEXT]

---

**Why this worksheet exists:**
The freeze is not random — it arrives in one of three forms for coaches in this programme, and each form has a different driver. The blank page freeze is almost always a perfectionism trigger dressed as a capability question. The rewrite spiral is almost always a trust deficit: you don't yet trust that your voice is enough, so you keep reaching for a version that sounds more like 'copy.' The post-publish regret is almost always a misfired comparison — you're reading your page through the eyes of a peer, not a prospect. Naming which one you're in stops the general panic and points you to the specific script that addresses it at the root.

tools.name: The Client-Psychology Reframe — Connecting Your Coaching Voice to Your Copy Voic
tools.instructions: Work through these five steps once, in order, before you write your next sales page or email — this is the session that proves to you that your coaching instincts and your copy ins
tools.content:
## The Client-Psychology Reframe SOP

A five-step working session that runs once before you write a new piece of copy. This is where the Client Psychology Reverse-Map meets the 'my brain doesn't write' belief directly — because the belief dissolves the moment you see that the skill you already have is the skill copy requires.

---

**What this session assumes:**
You have done at least one discovery call with a client who enrolled. That's the only raw material you need.

---

### Step 1 — Recall the exact moment the client said 'you completely get me'

Write it out from memory. Not the whole call — just the moment. The sentence they said. What you had just asked them or reflected back to them.

**Prompt:** *What did I say or ask in the thirty seconds before they said that?*

[WRITE YOUR ANSWER HERE]

---

### Step 2 — Identify the psychological move you made

Most coaches, when they replay this, find they did one of three things:

- Named the specific moment the client ran out of their own answer (not the general frustration — the exact moment)
- Reflected back a feeling the client had named only obliquely, and named it precisely
- Connected two things the client had said ten minutes apart, showing them a pattern they hadn't seen

**Circle which one you did. If it was something else, write it below.**

[WRITE YOUR ANSWER HERE]

---

### Step 3 — Translate that move into the opening paragraph of your sales page

This is the Client Psychology Reverse-Map in practice. The move you made on the call — the one that produced 'you completely get me' — is the same move your opening paragraph needs to make on the page. Not a description of your client's general pain. The specific moment.

**Fill in this template:**

> There's a moment — usually mid-sentence, often in a conversation you've had a hundred times — where [DESCRIBE THE SPECIFIC MOMENT YOUR CLIENT HITS THE WALL IN ONE SENTENCE]. It's not burnout. It's not imposter syndrome. It's [NAME THE PRECISE THING IT ACTUALLY IS, IN YOUR VOICE]. That's the moment this programme starts from.

---

### Step 4 — Read the paragraph back and ask: 'Would I say this on a call?'

If yes: it's your voice. This is copy.
If no: find the sentence that sounds like you borrowed it from someone else's page. Rewrite that sentence only in the words you'd use on a call.

**Note the sentence you rewrote:**

[WRITE IT HERE — ORIGINAL THEN REVISED]

---

### Step 5 — Carry this paragraph into the programme

This is your opening paragraph for your sales page. Bring it to the next live session or coaching call inside the programme and use it as the starting point for the full reverse-map exercise. You are not starting from a blank page — you are starting from a paragraph written in your voice, built from a real moment you already know how to find.

**What to bring:** The paragraph from Step 3 and the psychological move you identified in Step 2.

---

**Why this SOP exists:**
The 'my brain doesn't write' belief survives because coaches keep trying to write copy by learning copy — consuming frameworks, studying other pages, editing and re-editing. The Client Psychology Reverse-Map works backwards: it starts from the coaching move you already make brilliantly, and shows you that the move IS the copy. This SOP is the bridge between those two things. Do it once and the belief has nowhere left to stand.

tools.name: The 17-Script Bank — Expanded (All Sections, All Scripts)
tools.instructions: This is the complete bank — all seventeen scripts across all three stuck moments. Dog-ear the section you use most often.
tools.content:
## SECTION 1 — The Blank Page
### Scripts 1–6: When nothing is written yet and the cursor is winning

---

**Script 1 — The Discovery Call Redirect**
"I already know how to find the moment that makes a prospect feel seen. That's the only thing this sentence needs to do. What's the moment?"

*Use when: You're staring at an opening paragraph and nothing is coming.*

---

**Script 2 — The Permission Script**
"The first draft is not copy. The first draft is notes from someone who knows their client. I am allowed to write bad sentences now and fix them after."

*Use when: You're trying to write a perfect first sentence and it's stopping you from writing any sentence.*

---

**Script 3 — The Voice Anchor**
"I will write this like I'm explaining it to [NAME ONE SPECIFIC CLIENT WHO GOT IT IMMEDIATELY]. Not to everyone. Just to them."

*Use when: The audience feels too large and abstract and the page feels like a performance.*

---

**Script 4 — The Expertise Reality Check**
"I have spent [NUMBER] years understanding what my clients need. I am not unqualified to write about this. I am the most qualified person alive to write about this specific thing."

*Use when: Imposter syndrome is showing up as a writing block.*

---

**Script 5 — The Format Reset**
"I don't have to write a sales page right now. I'm going to write three sentences about the moment my client hits the wall. Just those three sentences."

*Use when: The full page feels impossible and you need a smaller target.*

---

**Script 6 — The Stakes Reverse**
"The person who needs this programme is going to read this page. If I don't write it, they don't find me. Bad copy published beats perfect copy unwritten."

*Use when: Perfectionism is disguised as standards.*

---

## SECTION 2 — The Rewrite Spiral
### Scripts 7–12: When you've rewritten the same thing three or more times

---

**Script 7 — The Spiral Interrupt**
"I have now rewritten this sentence more times than my client will read it. I'm going to leave the current version and move to the next section."

*Use when: You are on rewrite four or more of the same sentence.*

---

**Script 8 — The Source Check**
"The reason this doesn't sound like me is because I've been editing it toward copy I've seen somewhere else. What would I actually say to [SPECIFIC CLIENT NAME]?"

*Use when: The copy feels professional but hollow — it doesn't sound like your voice.*

---

**Script 9 — The Enough Script**
"This sentence is accurate, specific, and in my voice. That is enough. A prospect who needs what I offer will recognise themselves in it."

*Use when: You keep polishing something that is already doing its job.*

---

**Script 10 — The Comparison Interrupt**
"I am not competing with that copywriter's page. I am writing for clients who chose me because I am not that copywriter. My voice is the differentiator, not the liability."

*Use when: You've opened a competitor's or a peer's sales page while editing your own.*

---

**Script 11 — The Proof Script**
"[CLIENT NAME] said '[EXACT QUOTE FROM A CLIENT WHO GOT YOU IMMEDIATELY]' after a discovery call where I used exactly these words. These words work."

*Use when: You've lost confidence in language you know from experience is right.*

---

**Script 12 — The Version Lock**
"I'm going to name this draft Final-V1 and close the document. The next version opens only after I have read it fresh, not while I am still in the session."

*Use when: You're cycling edits within the same sitting and getting further from the good version, not closer.*

---

## SECTION 3 — The Post-Publish Spiral
### Scripts 13–17: When it's live and the regret has arrived

---

**Script 13 — The Reader Reframe**
"My prospect is not reading this page the way I am reading it right now. They are reading it looking for themselves. If they find themselves, the copy worked."

*Use when: You're rereading a published page through the eyes of a peer and finding every flaw.*

---

nextStep.heading: Bring Script 3 and Your Step 3 Paragraph to Your Next Programme Session
nextStep.body: Your next move inside the programme is to take two things into your next live session or coaching call: the Voice Anchor script (Script 3, with your specific client's name filled in) and the opening paragraph you built in the Client-Psychology Reframe SOP. These two assets are your starting point for the full Client Psychology Reverse-Map exercise — you're not arriving empty-handed, you're arriving with a paragraph already written in your voice and a named anchor that proves the voice exists. Bring both to the session and let the programme build from there.
